note: US state automatic-renewal laws, for one plain line in a cancellation's steps when the user has told us their state. Each row was read on an official page (state code, session law, official bill PDF or attorney general page) and quotes the text it relies on. user_right is written to be true for any subscription the law covers, so it is hedged ('generally', 'most') where the law has limits; it is not legal advice and never promises a result. applies_when narrows when the line is shown: 'any', 'trial' (only while a free trial runs) or 'annual' (only for yearly or longer contracts). exclude_categories lists subscription categories the law exempts. Bills for internet, phone, insurance and utilities never get a state line, because these laws commonly exempt regulated utilities, telecom, cable and insurance. Federal: the FTC's 2024 click-to-cancel amendments were vacated on 2025-07-08 and are not in force (see federal.ftc_negative_option_rule); ROSCA still applies to subscriptions sold online.

rosca.law: Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act, 15 U.S.C. 8403
rosca.title: Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act (ROSCA)
rosca.rule: A seller that charges through an online negative option feature must disclose all material terms before taking billing information, get express informed consent before charging, and provide simple mechanisms for a consumer to stop recurring charges.
rosca.user_right: If you signed up online, federal law says the company must give you a simple way to stop the recurring charges.
rosca.quote: provides simple mechanisms for a consumer to stop recurring charges from being placed on the consumer's credit card, debit card, bank account, or other financial account.

ftc_negative_option_rule.status: No FTC click-to-cancel rule is in force. The 8th Circuit vacated the 2024 amendments on 2025-07-08 (Custom Communications, Inc. v. FTC). On 2026-02-12 the FTC restored the Negative Option Rule as it stood before 2024, which covers prenotification plans only. It published an advance notice of proposed rulemaking on 2026-03-13 (comments closed 2026-04-13); no proposed or final rule had followed by 2026-10-23.
ftc_negative_option_rule.notes: Federal Register API checked 2026-10-23: the 2026-02-12 final rule recodifies the pre-2024 text, and the 2026-03-13 document is an ANPRM. Never cite the 2024 click-to-cancel amendments as law.

states.name: California
states.law: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code 17600 to 17606 (17602 as amended by AB 2863, Stats. 2024, ch. 515)
states.title: California Automatic Renewal Law
states.rule: If the consumer accepted online, the business must let them cancel exclusively online, at will, without further steps that obstruct or delay immediate cancellation, through a prominent link or button or a pre-formatted cancellation email. There must also be a toll-free number, email, postal address or another easy mechanism.
states.user_right: If you signed up online, California law says the company must let you cancel online, at any time, without extra steps that block or delay you.
states.applies_to: Consumers in California. Exempts services regulated by the CPUC, FCC or FERC, insurance, alarm companies, banks and credit unions, and service contracts (17605).
states.quote: In addition to the requirements of subdivision (b), a business that allows a consumer to accept an automatic renewal or continuous service offer online shall allow a consumer to terminate the automatic renewal or continuous service exclusively online, at will, and without engaging any further steps that obstruct or delay the consumer's ability to terminate the automatic renewal or continuous service immediately.
states.notes: The live leginfo page blocks scripts (Cloudflare); the text was read from a 2026-09-23 Wayback copy of the official page. The AB 2863 version applies to contracts entered into, amended or extended on or after 2025-07-01; the online-cancellation sentence predates it.

states.name: New York
states.law: N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law 527-a (as amended by the 2025 budget, S.3008-C Part W)
states.title: New York Automatic Renewal Law
states.rule: The consumer must be able to cancel at any time with a simple mechanism that is as easy to use as the one used to consent, through the same medium, and through every medium the business accepts consent through. After a price increase without consent, the business must allow cancellation within at least 14 days after the charge with a pro rata refund.
states.user_right: New York law says the company must let you cancel at any time, the same way you signed up, and cancelling must be as easy as signing up.
states.applies_to: Individual consumers. Exempts services under a local franchise (such as cable), DFS-regulated entities, security alarm operators, banks and financial institutions, and service contract sellers.
states.price_increase_right: New York law also says that if the price went up without your consent, the company must let you cancel within at least 14 days of the new charge and refund the rest of the term.
states.quote: fail to provide the consumer with the option to cancel at any time using a simple cancellation mechanism that is as easy to use as the mechanism that the consumer used to provide consent and that is through the same medium that the consumer used to provide consent;
states.notes: Part W takes effect 180 days after the budget became law (signed 2025-05-09), about 2025-11-05; nysenate.gov shows the revision dated 2025-11-07. The price-increase wording (paragraph b-1: 'within, at least, fourteen days after such charge', pro rata refund) was read on the same page on 2026-10-23.

states.name: Colorado
states.title: Colorado automatic renewal contracts law
states.rule: The business must provide a simple, cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use and readily accessible cancellation mechanism. A one-step online cancellation link for consumers who signed up online is deemed to comply (a safe harbor, not a duty to offer online cancellation).
states.user_right: Colorado law says the company must give you a simple, timely and easy-to-use way to cancel.
states.applies_to: Exempts utilities, cable and phone companies, insurers, banks, credit unions and airlines (AG FAQ).
states.quote: FAIL TO PROVIDE A SIMPLE, COST-EFFECTIVE, TIMELY, EASY-TO-USE, AND READILY ACCESSIBLE MECHANISM FOR CANCELING AN AUTOMATIC RENEWAL CONTRACT OR TRIAL PERIOD OFFER.
states.notes: Colorado's compiled statutes are not on a free official site, so the session law was read instead. Do not say Colorado requires online cancellation.

states.name: Illinois
states.title: Illinois Automatic Contract Renewal Act
states.rule: A consumer who accepted online must be allowed to cancel exclusively online, which may be a pre-formatted cancellation email or a link to a cancel page. There must also be a toll-free number, email, postal address or another easy mechanism.
states.user_right: If you signed up online, Illinois law says the company must let you cancel online.
states.applies_to: Not business-to-business contracts, banks and credit unions, certain cable and video providers, or insurance.
states.quote: A consumer who accepts an automatic renewal or continuous service offer online must be allowed to terminate the automatic renewal or continuous service exclusively online, which may include a termination email formatted and provided by the business that a consumer can send to the business without additional information, or a link to a website or other online service consumers can use to cancel.

states.name: Minnesota
states.title: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
states.rule: If the seller's website has profile or subscription management features, it must include a clear termination election that lets the consumer cancel at any time. For other sign-up methods, cancelling must be as easy as signing up. After a cancel request, save offers need the consumer's permission.
states.user_right: Minnesota law says that if the company's website lets you manage your subscription, it must also give you a clear way to cancel there at any time.
states.applies_to: Individual consumers. Exempts insurance licensees, services regulated by the PUC, FCC or FERC, and securities firms (325G.62).
states.quote: If a seller has a website with profile or subscription management capabilities, then such website must include a termination election on the website. The termination election must be clear and conspicuous on the website and must use plain language to convey that any consumer may use the termination election to terminate the agreement at any time.
states.notes: Applies to contracts entered into, modified or renewed on or after 2025-01-01.

states.name: Virginia
states.law: Va. Code 59.1-207.45 to 59.1-207.49 (as amended by 2026 Acts ch. 931 and 932)
states.title: Virginia automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
states.rule: The cancellation mechanism must be easy to find, at least as easy to use as the sign-up method, and available through at least each method by which the consumer could sign up.
states.user_right: If you signed up online, Virginia law says the company must let you cancel online too, and cancelling must be at least as easy as signing up.
states.applies_to: Individuals and small businesses. Exempts utilities, services regulated by the SCC, FCC or FERC, banks and credit unions, and insurers (59.1-207.48).
states.quote: 1. The cancellation mechanism shall be at least as easy to use as the mechanism the consumer used to initiate the automatic renewal or continuous service offer. 2. A seller shall provide a cancellation mechanism through, at a minimum, each of the methods by which a consumer may initiate an automatic renewal or continuous service offer, except for any such offer initiated in person, for which the provisions of subdivision 6 shall apply.
states.notes: Covers renewal terms of more than one month.

states.name: Oregon
states.title: Oregon automatic renewal and continuous service law
states.rule: The business must provide a toll-free number, email address, postal address (only when it bills directly) or another cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use way to cancel, described in the acknowledgment. There is no online-cancellation duty.
states.user_right: Oregon law says the company must give you an easy way to cancel, such as a toll-free number, an email address or another simple method.
states.applies_to: Individual consumers. Exempts regulated utilities and telecom, insurance, banks and credit unions, and satellite TV.
states.quote: A person making automatic renewal or continuous service offers shall provide a toll-free telephone number, electronic mail address, a post-office address only when the person directly bills the consumer, or another cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use mechanism for cancellation that must be described in the acknowledgment required by subsection (1)(c) of this section.
states.notes: Enacted by Or. Laws 2011 ch. 509; not amended since (2025 ORS edition). Original operative date not checked.

states.name: District of Columbia
states.law: D.C. Code 28A-203 (Automatic Renewal Protections Act of 2018)
states.title: DC Automatic Renewal Protections Act
states.rule: For a free trial of a month or more, the business must give notice 15 to 30 days before it ends and get the consumer's affirmative consent before charging for the renewal. There is no general online-cancellation duty.
states.user_right: For a free trial of a month or more, DC law says the company must get your consent before it starts charging you.
states.applies_to: Any person who buys or leases goods or services. Exempts insurers, banks and credit unions, regulated utilities and telecom, and service contracts.
states.quote: (2) Notwithstanding the consumer's consent to the free trial, obtain the consumer's affirmative consent to the automatic renewal before charging the consumer for the automatic renewal.
states.notes: The official code pages' applicability notes conflict (28A-203 says the funding condition was removed; 28A-202 and 28A-204 still carry a 'not implemented' note). Shown only while a free trial runs.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.law: 940 CMR 38.05 (Attorney General regulation under M.G.L. c. 93A)
states.title: Massachusetts recurring charges and trial offers regulation
states.rule: The business must provide a simple mechanism to cancel and immediately stop recurring charges, at least as easy to use as the sign-up method and available at least through the same medium; for internet sign-ups, on the same website or app.
states.user_right: If you signed up online, Massachusetts rules say the company must let you cancel on the same website or app, at least as easily as you signed up.
states.applies_to: Offers to people in Massachusetts buying for personal, family or household use.
states.quote: For any Product with a Negative Option Feature, failing to provide a simple mechanism for a consumer to cancel the Negative Option Feature and avoid being charged for the Product and immediately stop any recurring charges. (a) The simple mechanism required by 940 CMR 38.05(3) must be at least as easy to access and use as the method the consumer used to initiate the Negative Option Feature.
states.notes: A regulation, not a statute. mass.gov blocks scripts; read from a 2026-04-01 Wayback copy of the official PDF. Later amendments not checked.

states.name: Vermont
states.title: Vermont consumer contracts automatic renewal law
states.rule: For contracts with an initial term of one year or longer that renew for more than a month: if the consumer accepted online, the seller must permit cancellation exclusively online, which may be a pre-formatted cancellation email.
states.user_right: For a contract of a year or longer that you accepted online, Vermont law says the seller must let you cancel online.
states.applies_to: Only contracts with an initial term of one year or longer. Excludes financial institutions, credit unions and insurance.
states.quote: (2) if the consumer accepted the contract online, permit the consumer to terminate the contract exclusively online, which may include a termination e-mail formatted and provided by the seller or lessor that the consumer can send without additional information.
states.notes: Monthly subscriptions are not covered, so the line is shown only for yearly contracts. The date the online clause took effect was not confirmed.

states.name: Connecticut
states.law: Conn. Gen. Stat. 42-158ff (as amended by P.A. 25-44 and P.A. 25-113)
states.title: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
states.rule: A business that enters into the agreement online must let the consumer stop the renewal or service online, without requiring any offline step, through a prominent link or button, a reply email or (from 2026-07-01) a phone number shown on its website.
states.user_right: If you signed up online, Connecticut law says most companies must let you cancel online, with no offline step.
states.applies_to: Connecticut-resident individuals. Excludes regulated utilities and telecom, insurance, banks and credit unions, and any national service largely made of audiovisual content (such as major video streaming services).
states.quote: Each business that enters into a consumer agreement online shall, if such agreement includes an automatic renewal provision or a continuous services provision, allow the consumer to take any action necessary to prevent such automatic renewal or prevent or terminate such continuous consumer services online and without requiring such consumer to take any offline action to prevent such automatic renewal or prevent or terminate such continuous consumer services.
states.notes: Online-cancellation duty covers agreements entered into or amended on or after 2023-10-01; the current version took effect 2026-07-01. Not shown for video streaming, which is likely exempt.

states.name: Delaware
states.title: Delaware consumer contracts automatic renewal law
states.rule: For any automatically renewing contract, the seller must provide a cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use cancellation mechanism, and a consumer who entered into the contract online must be permitted to cancel online.
states.user_right: If you signed up online, Delaware law says the seller must let you cancel online.
states.applies_to: Individual consumers. Excludes contracts over $50,000, banks and utility tariffs.
states.quote: With respect to a contract that automatically renews and without regard to the duration of such renewal period, fails to provide a cost-effective, timely, and easy to use mechanism for cancellation. A consumer who enters into a contract online shall be permitted to cancel the contract online.
states.notes: Later amended by 84 Del. Laws c. 233 (not opened).
